newsitem.title: USA: CFTC proposes further easing on rule reviews.
newsitem.headline: CFTC proposes further easing on rule reviews.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposed relaxing its procedures involving reviews of contract market rules that do not relate to contract terms.

The proposal is part of the CFTC's ongoing effort to streamline regulations to reduce regulatory burdens and delays for markets and persons regulated by the agency, CFTC chairwoman Brooksley Born said at a CFTC meeting Tuesday.
Futures exchange leaders and industry officials at a news conference in Chicago on Monday pointed to U.S. regulations as the number one threat to their business.
Even with the easing, the CFTC will continue to ensure that the public is protected against fraud in the futures markets, Born said.

The CFTC's action follows its proposal last month to create a "fast-track" review by revising procedures relating to contract terms. That proposal would cut the CFTC's approval period for proposed contract market rules to between 45 and 75 days, from the current 180 days.
In its latest proposal, the CFTC would deem a proposed rule change approved, or placed into effect without approval, 10 days after the proposal is made.
The CFTC's review period could stretch to 45 days if the agency sought more time to consider the rule, or to 75 days if the rules were published for comment in the Federal Register.
The review could be even longer if the contract market agreed to another specified period.

At the end of the review period, a proposed rule would be deemed approved without further CFTC action unless the agency began disapproval proceedings, or the contract market withdrew the proposal or requested an extension of the review period to the current 180 days.
The CFTC said it would entertain comments from the public for 30 days on the rule-making proposal.
